title: Tech English — casos reales
description: Inglés técnico del día a día: standups, code reviews, on-call/incident, PR descriptions, architecture reviews, entrevistas técnicas. Frases y vocabulario que un ingeniero senior debe reconocer y usar con naturalidad.

vocab.example: I have a blocker on the auth flow — waiting on the mobile team.
Can you unblock me on the review by Friday?
Tests are green — let's ship it.
We had to revert the deployment due to a regression.
This test is flaky — it passes locally but fails on CI.
Nit: prefer const over let here.
LGTM — feel free to merge.
This is WIP, please don't review yet.
Deploying a hotfix for the checkout bug.
I'm on-call this week, ping me if the alerts go off.
I got paged at 3am for a database spike.
Let's write a blameless postmortem tomorrow.
The root cause was a race condition in the retry logic.
For now, we're using a workaround — proper fix next sprint.
We took on tech debt to hit the launch date.
Let me rubber duck this with you for a minute.
I'll do a quick spike to see if GraphQL fits our use case.
This is a breaking change — we need a major version bump.
We'll deprecate the v1 API next quarter.
We need a backfill job for the last 30 days.
We're doing a gradual rollout to 10% of users first.
The canary deploy caught the memory leak before full rollout.
It's behind a feature flag — we can toggle it off if needed.
The upstream is throttling our requests — we're hitting the rate limit.
Our p99 latency jumped from 100ms to 800ms.
Throughput dropped after we added encryption at rest.
I don't have bandwidth for another project this sprint.
Let's sync up after lunch to unblock this.
Action item: Sara to file the ticket by EOD.

vocab.translation: End Of Day (fin de la jornada)
vocab.example: Can you push the fix by EOD?
What's your ETA on the migration script?
Our SLA is 99.9% availability.
The SLO is stricter than the SLA to give us buffer.
The frontend falls back to cache — graceful degradation.
That auth service is a single point of failure — we need HA.

listening.text: Quick update from my side: I'm blocked on the API contract, waiting on Sara. Aiming to unblock today.
We just got paged for elevated error rates on the payments service. Investigating now.
The p99 latency spiked to two seconds — we're rolling back the last deploy to confirm.
Left a few nits and one blocking comment on your PR — nothing major, mostly readability.
Let's timebox this discussion to fifteen minutes and take the rest offline.
The root cause was a race condition in the retry logic — we filed a follow-up ticket.
I'd push back on that scope — let's keep the MVP tight and iterate after launch.
Can you rubber duck this with me for a minute? Something's not adding up.

speaking.target: Quick standup update: yesterday I finished the auth refactor; today I'm on the migration script; no blockers.
I have a concern about coupling the checkout to the inventory service directly — we should decouple with events.
Let me push back on that: the trade-off isn't worth it — we'd be paying for scale we don't need.
The alert fired because the queue backed up — we're throttling the consumer while we scale the workers.
Explain in one sentence what a circuit breaker does and why you'd use one.
You're in a design review. Justify why you'd choose a queue over synchronous HTTP for this workflow.
You just merged a hotfix. Draft a one-line message to post in #incidents summarizing what you did.
